title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 5th District
area: Northern New Jersey, including all or part of Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex counties.

context.text: Incumbent Josh Gottheimer ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote. Sean Kirrane won the Republican primary unopposed after Chandiha Gajapathy withdrew.
The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rates the district D+2.

summary.text: Josh Gottheimer is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2016 after a career as a Clinton White House speechwriter and in the private sector, at the Federal Communications Commission, and at Microsoft. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is Vice-Chair of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, and co-chairs the SALT Caucus. He sought the Democratic nomination for governor in 2025.

background.text: Born in Livingston, in Essex County, New Jersey, in 1975, and graduated from West Essex Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 2004; between them he studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, on a Thouron Award.

Worked as a speechwriter for President Bill Clinton from 1998 to 2001, including on two State of the Union addresses, and later worked on the presidential campaigns of Wesley Clark and John Kerry in 2004.
Worked in corporate communications at Ford Motor Company and at the public relations firm Burson-Marsteller before joining the Federal Communications Commission in 2010.
Served as senior counselor to the chairman of the FCC and later as a general manager for corporate strategy at Microsoft before running for Congress.
Won the 5th District seat in November 2016, defeating seven-term Republican incumbent Scott Garrett, 51.1% to 46.7%; he was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024.
Serves in Congress on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he is ranking member of the National Security Agency and Cyber Subcommittee, and on the Financial Services Committee.

Helped launch the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus in 2017 and served as co-chair during the 115th through 118th Congresses; now Vice-Chair, and co-chair of the SALT Caucus and the Law Enforcement Caucus.
Announced a run for governor of New Jersey in November 2024 and placed fourth in the June 10, 2025 Democratic primary with 11.8% of the vote.

priorities.text: Helped launch the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus in 2017 and now serves as its Vice-Chair, working across party lines on taxes, the environment, healthcare affordability, national security, and infrastructure.
Co-chairs the bipartisan SALT Caucus, which pushes to restore the state and local tax deduction, and the Law Enforcement Caucus.

positions.summary: In an October 2025 release, called for extending the Affordable Care Act premium tax credits set to expire at the end of that year.
positions.quote: I’m hopeful that Republicans will come to the table, work with us to reopen the government, and extend these critical ACA premium tax credits.

record.text: Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security Agency and Cyber and a member of the Subcommittee on Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture, and on the House Financial Services Committee, including its Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions and Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence.
Announced introduction of the bipartisan Kylie's Voices for Childhood Cancer Act ("Kylie's Law") with Rep. Mike Lawler (NY-17) during Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.
Introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with Rep. Mike Lawler, legislation intended to establish guardrails for AI "agents" operating on computer networks.
The House passed the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, a bill Gottheimer says he first championed, requiring automakers to include AM radio in new vehicles.
The House passed the bipartisan, Gottheimer-led GUARD Act, aimed at protecting seniors from financial fraud and scammers.

candidates.name: Sean Kirrane
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed after the withdrawal of Chandiha Gajapathy.

summary.text: Sean Kirrane is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District. Born in Westwood and now living in River Vale, he is a corporate consultant and entrepreneur who began his career in banking and says he has more than twenty years of experience in healthcare, finance, and technology. He has not previously run for office and describes himself as a "socially moderate, fiscally responsible" Republican focused on affordability, healthcare, and housing.

background.text: Born in Westwood, New Jersey; earned a high school diploma from Bergen Catholic High School and a bachelor's degree from St. Joseph's University in 2000. Also attended Villanova University.

Says his first job was a summer internship at Hudson United Bancorp during college, after which he stayed on and, by his account, rose to Assistant Vice President of Treasury Operations within a few years.
Career experience as an entrepreneur and executive; as of 2025 was affiliated with Cortex-X, the Kirrane Group, and Arcadia Health Partners.
Describes more than twenty years working in healthcare, finance and technology, including leading what he calls billion-dollar transactions and turnarounds of bankrupt hospitals.
The New Jersey Globe described him in September 2025 as a corporate consultant, artificial intelligence entrepreneur, and father of two from River Vale who had never run for office.
Announced his candidacy for the Republican nomination in September 2025, saying he would focus on affordable housing legislation and a universal health care system driven by the free market.

priorities.text: "Government should do fewer things — and do them well," proposing to cap administrative costs at 10% across federal programs and eliminate waste.
priorities.quote: Government should do fewer things — and do them well.

priorities.text: Housing, through what he calls the American Citizens' Primary Residence Mortgage Act to protect homeownership for U.S. citizens.
Healthcare, through what he calls the American Citizens' Health Insurance Act, which he says would guarantee affordable baseline coverage while preserving free-market choice.
Homelessness, through what he calls the Homeless Solutions and Stability Act, replacing what he describes as unsafe shelters with treatment-based recovery programs.

statements.quote: The American Citizens’ Health Insurance Act brings fiscal discipline to universal coverage.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Statements and priorities are from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His campaign website (kirraneforcongress.com) returned a Cloudflare bot check and could not be read. No statements found on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement or the other listed issues.

candidates.name: Adam Rueda

summary.text: Adam Rueda is the Humane Sustainable Future Party candidate for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District. A Bucknell University graduate and former financial analyst who described himself in a 2025 survey as 28 years old, he says he co-founded a new political party, "greenparty2.0," focused on environmental and health policy, gun-control reform, and campaign-finance and lobbying reform.

background.text: Raised in Andover Township (Sussex County); attended Catholic grade and middle school and graduated from Pope John XXIII Regional High School in Sparta.

Earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, with a focus in financial management and accounting, from Bucknell University in 2019; says he was a first-generation college graduate, vice president of his fraternity, and a participant in the university's Student Managed Investment Fund.

Has worked as a senior financial analyst at a commercial real estate brokerage in Morristown, as an interior design salesperson in Short Hills and Manhattan, and as a DJ in New York City and Brooklyn.
Says he is one of 11 executive committee chairs of greenparty2.0, a party he describes as led by young professionals and activists. He has not held elected office.

priorities.text: Says he co-founded "greenparty2.0," a party he describes as led by "Earth-first, health-first" young activists, focused on environmental and health policy.
Supports stricter gun-control measures, including reform to gun storage requirements and additional steps, such as mental-health evaluations, before purchase.

Says lobbying and campaign contributions from the fossil-fuel industry and pro-Israel groups like AIPAC improperly influence sitting members of Congress, and supports campaign-finance and election reform, including open primaries.

positions.summary: Supports stricter gun-storage requirements and additional screening, including mental-health evaluations, before firearm purchases, and wants to limit access to assault weapons.
positions.quote: Our party is passionate about thinking creatively about gun control, which could include reform to gun storage req., increasing hoops to get a gun, including mental health evaluations, as well as limiting access to assault weapons.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. should divest from fossil fuels and move swiftly on green-energy solutions to address ecosystem degradation and intensifying storms.
positions.quote: This can be addressed by divesting from fossil fuels and exploring science, research and acting swiftly to implement green solutions.
